transcript:
[00:00] Jordan (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for jumping on. I'm Jordan from Redwood, AE for StrataFold account. With me is Priya, our solutions engineer. How's everybody doing?
[00:09] Maya (StrataFold): Good thanks, excited. We've got about 45 minutes, right?
[00:12] Jordan: Yup planning for ~45. We want to run through a quick SDK install and auth flow, show the Console, and give some Optimize suggestions for your ingestion workload. Priya will do the code bits.
[00:22] Priya (Redwood SE): Hi all. I'll try to keep it pragmatic — two quick samples, Python and TypeScript, then show the Console where you map environments to models and configure batching.
[00:30] Liam (StrataFold): Quick note — we care a lot about latency tail and cost. Our users are live chat agents so 99th percentile matters. Also we have a VPC requirement for some datasets.
[00:40] Priya: Totally understood. We'll call out latency SLOs and dedicated/private options.
[00:44] Jordan: Quick qual: what's your current LLM infra? Are you using hosted APIs or self-hosted?
[00:50] Maya: Mostly OpenAI for prototyping, some internal endpoints on a managed k8s cluster. We have SSO via Okta (SAML) and key rotation policy.
[00:58] Priya: Good to know. Redwood supports API keys for quickstart and SAML/OIDC for enterprise SSO; for Private we can integrate your IdP metadata.
[01:05] Cara (StrataFold SRE): Also curious about audit logs and KMS — we need customer-managed keys for certain projects.
[01:11] Jordan: Yep, KMS/HSM integrations are supported on Private and we have a key-rotation pattern for Dedicated. We'll share the security pack after.
[01:18] Priya: Ok I'll share my screen — starting with the Python quickstart. The pip package is redwood-inference (note: docs sometimes show redwood-client in older examples, ignore that). Run: pip install redwood-inference.
[01:30] [murmur] Liam: pip install... got it.
[01:33] Priya: Then auth — simplest path is export REDWOOD_API_KEY="<sandbox-key>". For SAML/OIDC we set up SSO via the Console and exchange a short-lived token. On Private you'll use your IdP metadata and our connector.
[01:45] Priya: Code snippet —
[01:48] Priya: from redwood import Client
[01:50] Priya: client = Client()
[01:52] Priya: resp = client.generate("Write a short reply to a customer about billing delay")
[01:56] Priya: print(resp.text)
[01:58] Maya: That looks straightforward. Any special env vars for batching?
[02:02] Priya: Batching is configured server-side per route but you can hint via a client param. In Python you'd do Client(batch=True, batch_hint_size=8) — but the Console is where you tune continuous batching vs low-latency mode.
[02:14] Jordan: For TypeScript it's npm i @redwood/inference and similar API.
[02:19] Priya: Right. Then we switched to the Console — Projects view: you can create a "staging" project mapped to a hosted model, and a "prod" project mapped to Dedicated GPU pool. You can pin model versions and set rollout policies.
[02:30] [00:02:30] Jordan: On the Console screenshot I showed, note the per-route token cost breakdown and latency histograms — those are super helpful when tuning.
[02:38] Liam: Is there a way to see per-token cost at the prompt vs generation split?
[02:41] Priya: Yep, Console shows token split and you can export a CSV. We also surface how much KV cache hit rate you're getting if you enable prefix caching.
[02:49] Cara: About VPC: do requests stay on your control plane or is data egressed? We need to keep data inside our VPC.
[02:58] Jordan: For Private deployments, the control plane can be customer-managed and inference stays within VPC; for Redwood Hosted, payloads hit our control plane — we have contractual NDAs and SOC2 but if residency is required, Private is the path.
[03:12] Priya: Switching back to dev: showing the sample TS code —
[03:16] Priya: import { RedwoodClient } from '@redwood/inference'
[03:19] Priya: const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY })
[03:23] Priya: const r = await client.generate({ model: 'rw-llama-7b', prompt: 'Summarize this support ticket' })
[03:31] [small coughs] Maya: Two quick questions — first, about caching: will prefix caching leak PII between tenants?
[03:37] Priya: Good question. Caching is configurable per-project and per-route; we can disable caching for PII-sensitive routes. For multi-tenant setups you can scope caches to a tenant namespace. Also we scrub prompts in flight if you enable strict pii masking.
[03:50] Liam: Second — what quantization options are recommended? We have latency constraints but limited GPU budget.
[03:55] Priya: For many of our customers, 4-bit quantization on compatible models gives a 2–4x inference speedup with small quality drop for generative QA; Optimize will flag suggested quantization profiles per model and workload.
[04:06] Jordan: We also showed a small Optimize recommendation card — suggests increasing batch size for stable prompts and enabling KV cache for repeated prefix-heavy chats.
[04:13] [00:04:13] Cara: On compliance: do you produce audit logs that can be forwarded to our SIEM?
[04:18] Priya: Yes, audit logs and token-level tracing are exportable via S3 or a logging endpoint; we can stream to Splunk/Datadog.
[04:24] Maya: Great. Can you run a quick end-to-end demo? From npm install to a generate call using the sandbox key?
[04:29] Priya: Sure — I'll paste the quickstart repo link in chat (https://redwood.ai/quickstarts/devtools — note this is a shorthand link, full link will be in follow-up).
[04:37] [screen share: terminal]
[04:40] Priya: npm i @redwood/inference
[04:42] Priya: export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk_sandbox_...
[04:45] Priya: node run example.js
[04:47] [terminal noise, typing sounds] Priya: And you can see the response returned in ~120ms on this sandbox. Your mileage depends on model and route.
[04:58] Liam: 120ms is great — what's the 99th on prod for that model on Dedicated?
[05:02] Priya: Typical 99th for rw-llama-7b on Dedicated is ~250–350ms with optimized kernels and small batch sizes; if you push batching it'll increase throughput but tail might move. We'll run a bench with your prompts to get exact numbers.
[05:13] Jordan: We should set that as an action — Priya to run a 1k-prompt bench.
[05:16] Priya: noted.
[05:18] [00:05:18] Maya: Another practical thing — CI secrets: do you have recommended ways to inject keys for ephemeral environments?
[05:25] Priya: We recommend our CI secret helper or storing in your cloud secret manager and rotating keys; for longer-lived infra we recommend short-lived OIDC tokens via your IdP. We'll send our CI snippets.
[05:34] Cara: For Private, how much ops effort is required? We're cautious about running stateful infra.
[05:39] Jordan: Our Private package is turnkey — we provide Terraform modules and an operator; the handoff includes an sprints-based runbook. You still need to provision GPUs and network but Redwood supports upgrade automation. We'll share the onboarding deck.
[05:52] Maya: We've also got legal review — any standard terms around data retention for hosted?
[05:56] Jordan: Hosted default retention is 30 days for logs, but we have stricter retention options and can commit via contract. We'll put the retention options in the security pack.
[06:05] [00:06:05] Priya: Quick note on dev ergonomics — Console has a "local proxy" feature so devs can point local SDK to a proxied staging model without exposing prod keys. That helps iterate safely.
[06:15] Liam: Nice. Is there a way to do A/B testing at the routing layer?
[06:18] Priya: Yes, Route rollouts let you do canary and A/B with percentage splits and automatic fallback if errors spike. Metrics include per-route latency, token cost, and qualitative eval bucketing if you push eval sets.
[06:32] Jordan: Let's do a 2-minute recap and next steps.
[06:34] Jordan: Recap — we walked through pip/npm quickstarts, auth options (API key for sandbox, SAML/OIDC for SSO), Console mapping for envs, Optimize suggestions, and Private options for VPC and KMS. Action items are in the chat and I'll follow up via email.
[06:49] Maya: Sounds good. Quick ask — can you send a sample terraform to provision a sandbox Dedicated pool? We want to try Dedicated for a short POC.
[06:57] Priya: Yes, Priya will share a terraform starter and a minimal infra template for a 1-GPU Dedicated pool.
[07:03] Jordan: OK we'll leave the recording and the quickstart link in the calendar invite. Anything else?
[07:07] Cara: No that's it from infra side. Thanks.
[07:09] Maya: Thanks everyone.
[07:11] Jordan: Thanks, we'll follow up with the security docs and the sandbox creds.
[07:15] [END]

Notes: transcript contains some minor mis-transcriptions (package name alternatives mentioned, short pauses). References shared in chat: quickstart repo link (redwood.ai/quickstarts/devtools), security pack link (to be sent).
